messages:
emma-support: Heads-up: Acme reporting widespread latency and some 504s after today's canary runtime push, started ~2026-03-15T16:18Z.
acme-api-team: Repro from our side — app started getting 504s at 16:21Z. Sample curl:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme" -H "x-tenant: acme-prod-3" -d '{"input":"summarize ..."}'
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```
nate-runtime: Which image did we roll? deploy-bot, can you paste the canary metadata?
deploy-bot: rollout.event: runtime:v2.14 -> cohort:acme-prod; percent:15; started_at:2026-03-15T16:18:32Z
tom-oncall: Alerting: correlated p95/p99 rise and tenant auth refresh 429s at ~16:19-16:22Z. Seeing spikes on routing mesh.
marco-sre: Quick stats from metrics: cohort acme-prod p95 110ms -> 450ms, p99 300ms -> 2.05s. Error-rate (504/502) up ~3x.
emma-support: Customer also saw duplicate billing attempts during the window — probably retries, but logging it to the ticket.
nate-runtime: v2.14 included kernel-selector tweaks and an experimental batched-attn kernel. My hunch: interacting badly with cold KV cache on auth refresh path.
selena-oncall: Immediate mitigations we can do now:
- pause rollout to other cohorts (done)
- route current acme traffic back to v2.13
- temporarily extend auth-token TTL for that tenant (if safe)
marco-sre: I can reproduce a p99 tail locally if I run concurrent streams and force auth refresh churn + cold KV eviction. Looks like a long synchronous path during kvcache eviction.
emma-support: Acme sent a sanitized trace and headers: concurrency ~28, seq len 512, auth refresh cadence ~5s (their proxy).
nate-runtime: Please attach that trace to the ticket; I'll have runtime-quant run the same pattern against v2.14 staging.
marco-sre: Bisect plan: isolate commits touching `kvcache`, `kernel-scheduler`, and `batched-attn`. Start with `git bisect` between v2.13 and v2.14 for kvcache_migrator changes.
selena-oncall: Actioned: traffic switch executed at 2026-03-15T16:40Z — acme routed to runtime:v2.13. Monitoring shows p99 back down to ~360ms within 3 minutes; 504s cleared.
acme-api-team: Confirmed — errors and billing anomalies stopped. Latency back to baseline. Thank you.
emma-support: Ticket #ACME-8123 opened for postmortem, billing credit, and follow-ups. tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre for RCA + patch.
nate-runtime: Assigned to runtime-quant for root cause + hotfix; will aim for initial findings in ~2 hours.
marco-sre: Saved graphs and logs: https://internal.redwood/metrics/cohort/acme-prod/2026-03-15
selena-oncall: If hotfix takes >24h, keep canary paused and block further rollouts. Otherwise we can test targeted patch on canary cohort only. :thumbsup:
emma-support: Notifying customer of rollback and credit. Closing this thread; will reopen if any regression.
